mainTopic: Completeness of the משנה's fast-day list, where to say עננו, pregnant and nursing women on fasts, and what הַתְרָעָה means
overview: The גמרא first asks whether the משנה's list for the last seven fasts leaves anything out. It shows that the תיבה and the twenty-four blessings are not real omissions, because the תנא teaches them in the next פרק. Then it asks where an individual adds עננו in the עמידה, and rules that it goes in שומע תפילה. Next, three ברייתות disagree about whether pregnant and nursing women fast. רב אשי settles this by saying they fast only on the middle three fasts. The גמרא then asks what 'sounding the alarm' (מתריעין) on the last seven fasts means. One opinion says it means שופרות, and another says it means the prayer עננו. In the end, everyone agrees that שופרות count, and the argument is only whether עננו is also called הַתְרָעָה. A משנה about sounding the alarm on שבת shows that some תנא does call prayer הַתְרָעָה. The amud ends by starting a story about a time of trouble in the days of רבי יהודה נשיאה, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ark was left out too
steps.stepSummary: Someone points out that the תנא also left out the rule of the תיבה, so the משנה's list is not complete.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he left out the ark!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to another rule the משנה did not mention: the תיבה (ark) that was carried out into the street on the later fasts. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תנא skipped the תיבה, that suggests the משנה's list is not meant to be complete. It would mean the תנא does leave things out (תנא ושייר).

keyTerms.meaning: the ark holding the ספר תורה, brought outside on the stricter fasts
the תנא taught a list but left items out

phrases.english: But he left out the ark!
phrases.notes: The ark was carried into the town square on the last seven fasts; the משנה here never mentions it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא שַׁיַּיר תֵּיבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of whether the משנה's list is complete.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה lists everything that differs on the later fasts.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A known rule (the תיבה) is missing, so the list must have gaps.

steps.title: Public matters are not listed here
steps.stepSummary: Leaving out the תיבה is not a real omission. The תנא here lists only private matters, not public ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is because of the ark, that is not an omission. He teaches private matters; he does not teach public matters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: the תיבה does not count as something left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא in this list is only covering private matters (מילי דצינעא). The תיבה ceremony happens in public (בפרהסיא), so it was never meant to be part of this list. Its absence proves nothing.

phrases.aramaic: אִי מִשּׁוּם תֵּיבָה — לָאו שִׁיּוּרָא הוּא.
phrases.english: If it is because of the ark, that is not an omission.
He teaches matters done in private,
he does not teach matters done in public.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מִשּׁוּם תֵּיבָה לָאו שִׁיּוּרָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the challenge of step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The תיבה cannot be used as proof that the list has gaps.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The list only covers private matters, so a public ceremony was never supposed to be on it.

steps.title: רב אשי: the משנה's wording supports this
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the משנה's wording 'מה אלו יתירות' shows it is giving a complete list of differences.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The משנה is precise too, since it teaches: How are these more than the first ones? Only that on these they sound the alarm and lock the stores. But in all their other matters, both are the same.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings support from the exact wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה asks 'how are these more strict than the earlier ones' and gives specific differences. It then adds that in everything else they are the same. That sounds like a full list, not a list with gaps.

keyTerms.meaning: is precise; its wording supports this
they sound the alarm (blow שופרות/cry out)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: מַתְנִיתִין נָמֵי דַּיְקָא,
phrases.english: רב אשי said: The משנה is also precise,

phrases.aramaic: דְּקָתָנֵי: מָה אֵלּוּ יְתֵירוֹת עַל הָרִאשׁוֹנוֹת,
phrases.english: as it teaches: How are these more strict than the first ones?
phrases.notes: 'These' are the last seven fasts; 'the first ones' are the earlier fasts.

phrases.english: Only that on these they sound the alarm
and they lock the stores.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּכׇל דִּבְרֵיהֶן — זֶה וָזֶה שָׁוִין.
phrases.english: But in all their other matters, both are the same.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי מַתְנִיתִין נָמֵי דַּיְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the answer in step 2 with the משנה's wording.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה is not simply leaving things out.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's phrase 'מה אלו יתירות על הראשונות... אבל בכל דבריהן זה וזה שוין'.

steps.title: Blocking the 'he just left it out' reply
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי heads off a reply: you can't say the תנא left things out here, because he says 'מה אלו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that here too he taught and left out, but it teaches 'how are these'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי finishes his proof by blocking a possible way out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might say this משנה is also one where the תנא lists some items and skips others. רב אשי answers that the phrase 'מה אלו' signals a complete comparison. So that excuse does not work here.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָכָא נָמֵי תְּנָא וְשַׁיַּיר,
phrases.english: And if you say that here too he taught and left out,
but it teaches 'how are these'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָכָא נָמֵי תְּנָא וְשַׁיַּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב אשי's proof by ruling out a counter-reading.
steps.raayaObject: That the list here is exact.

steps.title: Is 'מה אלו' really exact?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אשי: 'מה אלו' can't be exact, since the תיבה is still left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: And do you really think 'how are these' is exact? But he left out the ark!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב אשי's reading of the words 'מה אלו'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'מה אלו' means a complete list, then every difference should appear. Yet the תיבה, a real difference on the later fasts, is missing. So the wording can't be taken that strictly.

keyTerms.meaning: and do you really think so?

phrases.english: And do you really think 'how are these' is exact?
But he left out the ark!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִסְבְּרָא מָה אֵלּוּ דַּוְוקָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's proof.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's claim that 'מה אלו' means a complete list.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A complete list would include the תיבה, but it is missing.

steps.title: The ark is taught in another chapter
steps.stepSummary: The תיבה is not an omission because the תנא lists it in another פרק.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is because of the ark, that is not an omission, because he counts it in another chapter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a new reason the תיבה is missing here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the reason is not 'public vs. private'. Instead, the תנא already deals with the תיבה in the next פרק, so he did not need to repeat it here. So 'מה אלו' can still be exact.

phrases.aramaic: אִי מִשּׁוּם תֵּיבָה — לָאו שִׁיּוּרָא הוּא,
phrases.english: If it is because of the ark, that is not an omission,

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּקָא חָשֵׁיב לַהּ בְּאִידַּךְ פִּרְקָא.
phrases.english: because he counts it in the other chapter.
phrases.notes: This is the next פרק, where the משנה describes bringing the ark into the town square.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּקָא חָשֵׁיב לַהּ בְּאִידַּךְ פִּרְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The missing item is covered elsewhere, so it is not a real omission.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The missing תיבה shows the list has gaps.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא skips here only what he teaches in the other פרק.

steps.title: The twenty-four blessings are not an omission either
steps.stepSummary: Using the same answer, the twenty-four blessings also don't count as left out, since they are taught in the other פרק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have come to this: the twenty-four are also not an omission, since he teaches it in the other chapter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the answer it just gave and applies it to the earlier problem of the twenty-four blessings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier it seemed the משנה left out the twenty-four blessings of the fast-day תפילה. Now that we know the תנא skips items he teaches in the other פרק, the twenty-four blessings fit the same rule. So the משנה here does not really leave anything out.

keyTerms.meaning: now that you have come to this (answer)
the twenty-four blessings said on the stricter fasts

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's list ('מה אלו') is complete. Things missing from it, like the תיבה and the twenty-four blessings, are taught in the next פרק.

phrases.english: Now that you have come to this:

phrases.aramaic: עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה נָמֵי לָאו שִׁיּוּרָא הוּא,
phrases.english: the twenty-four are also not an omission,
phrases.notes: The twenty-four blessings: the regular eighteen plus six more added on these fasts.

phrases.english: since he teaches it in the other chapter.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָתֵית לְהָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the answer of step 6 to the earlier difficulty.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Neither the תיבה nor the twenty-four blessings show that the משנה leaves things out.

steps.title: What is the final ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the outcome is about where an individual inserts עננו.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the conclusion about it?
steps.whatsHappening: The proofs did not settle the question, so the גמרא asks for the bottom line. This sets up the opinions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The discussion was about an individual saying עננו on a fast. Since no proof decided it, the גמרא now asks where it actually goes in the עמידה.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the conclusion about it?

phrases.english: What is the conclusion about it?
phrases.notes: 'It' means the עננו prayer an individual adds on a fast day.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי הָוֵי עֲלַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion and returns to the practical question about עננו.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where in the עמידה an individual inserts עננו.

steps.title: First view: between גואל and רופא
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר סיסרטאי, and רב through רב חייא בר אשי, say עננו goes between גואל ישראל and רופא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר סיסרטאי said, and so said רב חייא בר אשי in the name of רב: Between 'Redeemer' and 'Healer'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first answer: עננו is placed as its own section between two blessings of the עמידה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This view places עננו right after the blessing of גואל ישראל and before רפאנו. In this view, עננו comes as a separate section between those two blessings.

phrases.english: רבי שמואל בר סיסרטאי said,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: and so said רב חייא בר אשי in the name of רב:
Between 'Redeemer' and 'Healer'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר סִסְרָטַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: עננו is said between גואל and רופא.

steps.title: Second view: in שומע תפילה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי, in the name of רבי ינאי son of רבי ישמעאל, says עננו is inserted in שומע תפילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב אשי said in the name of רבי ינאי son of רבי ישמעאל: In 'Who hears prayer'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different answer about where עננו goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here עננו is not its own section. Instead, it is said inside the blessing of שומע תפילה, the general blessing for requests.

phrases.english: And רב אשי said in the name of
רבי ינאי son of רבי ישמעאל:
In 'Who hears prayer'.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יַנַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing answer to step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: עננו is inserted within שומע תפילה.

steps.title: The הלכה: in שומע תפילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that an individual inserts עננו in שומע תפילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: in 'Who hears prayer'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא decides between the two views and gives the final הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הלכה follows the second view. An individual does not make a separate section for עננו; he includes it in שומע תפילה.
steps.whatToRemember: An individual on a fast day says עננו inside שומע תפילה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical ruling for where an individual adds עננו in the fast-day עמידה.

phrases.english: And the halacha is: in 'Who hears prayer'.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִלְכְתָא בְּשׁוֹמֵעַ תְּפִילָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between steps 9 and 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: עננו for an individual is said in שומע תפילה.

steps.title: Three teachings disagree about pregnant and nursing women
steps.stepSummary: Three ברייתות give three different rulings on whether עוברות ומיניקות fast on the first fasts, the last fasts, or neither.
steps.simpleTranslation: One ברייתא says pregnant and nursing women fast on the first fasts but not the last. A second says they fast on the last but not the first. A third says they fast on neither.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lines up three teachings that seem to clash. This sets up the next step, where someone will explain how they fit together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each ברייתא gives a different answer to the same question. No one says 'this is a problem' out loud, but placing them side by side works as a challenge: how can all three be true?

keyTerms.meaning: The first fasts / the last fasts

steps.confusionAlert: There are three sets of fasts for rain: the first three, the middle three, and the last seven. Keep all three sets in mind, or רב אשי's answer in the next step will not make sense.

phrases.english: It is taught in one ברייתא:
Pregnant and nursing women
fast on the first fasts,
but they do not fast on the last fasts.
And another ברייתא teaches:
They fast on the last fasts,
but they do not fast on the first fasts.
And yet another ברייתא teaches:
They do not fast,
neither on the first fasts nor on the last fasts.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי חֲדָא: עוּבָּרוֹת וּמֵינִיקוֹת מִתְעַנּוֹת בָּרִאשׁוֹנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the ruling about עננו.
steps.kashyaTarget: How the three ברייתות can all be true together
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The three sources give opposite rulings on the same case, so they seem to contradict each other.

steps.title: רב אשי: they fast on the middle fasts
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the rule is that עוברות ומיניקות fast on the middle set of fasts, and that this explains all three ברייתות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: hold on to the middle fasts, and then all three teachings work out.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the contradiction from the last step. He says the women fast only on the middle three fasts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'first' in the first ברייתא means the first of the two stricter sets, which is the middle set. The 'last' in the second ברייתא means the later of the first two sets, which is again the middle set. The third ברייתא means the real first three and the real last seven, and the women fast on neither of those.

keyTerms.meaning: Hold in your hand, meaning take this as the rule
The middle ones (the middle set of fasts)

steps.whatToRemember: עוברות ומיניקות fast only on the middle three fasts, and that one rule explains all three ברייתות.

phrases.english: רב אשי said:
Take the middle fasts in your hand,
phrases.notes: He means: treat the middle set of three fasts as the ones they keep.

phrases.english: since that resolves all of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: נְקוֹט אֶמְצָעֲיָיתָא בִּידָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction among the three ברייתות.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the sources so that 'first' and 'last' point to the same middle set
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The three ברייתות seemed to give three different rules.
steps.terutzMaskana: All three agree: the women fast only on the middle fasts.

steps.title: The משנה: on the last seven fasts they sound the alarm and close the shops
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: what makes the last seven fasts stricter is that they sound the alarm and lock the stores.
steps.simpleTranslation: How are these fasts stricter than the earlier ones? On these they sound the alarm and close the stores.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה. This sets up the question in the next step about what 'sounding the alarm' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה adds two things to the last seven fasts: מתריעין (sounding an alarm) and closing the shops. The word מתריעין is not explained in the משנה, so the גמרא will ask about it.

keyTerms.meaning: They sound an alarm, cry out

phrases.english: How are these stricter than the earlier ones?
phrases.notes: 'These' are the last seven fasts for rain.

phrases.english: Only that on these they sound the alarm
and they lock the stores.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה אֵלּוּ יְתֵירוֹת עַל הָרִאשׁוֹנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On the last seven fasts, they sound the alarm and lock the stores.

steps.title: What do they sound the alarm with?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'מתריעין' means in practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: With what do they sound the alarm?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple question: what exactly is used to sound the alarm? The next steps give two answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said 'מתריעין' without saying how. The question asks for the actual practice.

phrases.english: With what do they sound the alarm?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי מַתְרִיעִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a word in the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What 'מתריעין' means: what is used to sound the alarm.

steps.title: רב יהודה: with שופרות
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says the alarm is sounded with שופרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: with שופרות.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives the first answer: the alarm means blowing שופרות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this view, התרעה is a sound made with an instrument, the שופר. Another answer comes in the next step.

phrases.english: רב יהודה said:
With שופרות.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר: בְּשׁוֹפָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The alarm is sounded with שופרות.

steps.title: In the name of רב: with עננו
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה son of רב שמואל בר שילת, in the name of רב, says the alarm means saying the עננו prayer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה son of רב שמואל בר שילת said in the name of רב: with עננו.
steps.whatsHappening: A second answer: sounding the alarm means crying out in prayer with עננו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here התרעה is a spoken prayer, not a sound from a horn. So we now have two answers to the same question.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Answer us', a prayer added on fast days

steps.confusionAlert: There are two people named רב יהודה here. The first (step 16) speaks for himself; the second is the son of רב שמואל בר שילת and speaks in רב's name.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת
phrases.english: And רב יהודה, son of רב שמואל בר שילת,
said in the name of רב:
With עננו.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second, different answer to the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The alarm is the עננו prayer.

steps.title: First assumption: each side rejects the other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא assumes the עננו view does not allow שופרות, and the שופרות view does not allow עננו.
steps.simpleTranslation: We first thought: whoever says עננו does not say שופרות, and whoever says שופרות does not say עננו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states how it first understood the argument. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase קא סלקא דעתן marks a starting assumption, not a final ruling. The גמרא reads the two views as excluding each other, which opens the door to an attack.

keyTerms.meaning: It entered our mind, we first assumed

phrases.english: We first assumed
that the one who said 'with עננו'
does not say 'with שופרות,'
and the one who said 'with שופרות'
does not say 'with עננו.'

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets out how the two answers were first understood, to prepare a challenge.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First assumption: the two views exclude each other.

steps.title: Challenge from יריחו: the alarm was with שופרות
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says seven fasts with eighteen alarms, with יריחו as a memory sign; since יריחו had שופרות, this seems to refute the עננו view.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: no fewer than seven fasts are set for the public, with eighteen alarms among them, and the sign for this is יריחו. At יריחו there were שופרות, so this refutes the one who said עננו!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the עננו view, based on the assumption from the last step. The memory sign יריחו points to שופרות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא ties the fast-day alarms to יריחו, where the walls fell to the sound of שופרות. If the alarm were only the עננו prayer, why use יריחו as the sign? So the עננו view, read as rejecting שופרות, seems to be disproven.

keyTerms.meaning: They do not set fewer than
A memory sign for the matter

steps.confusionAlert: The refutation only works because of the assumption in step 18, that the עננו view rejects שופרות. It is not a final ruling against רב.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין מִשֶּׁבַע תַּעֲנִיּוֹת עַל הַצִּבּוּר,
phrases.english: They do not set fewer than seven fasts on the public,
which include eighteen alarms.
And a sign for this is יריחו.
phrases.notes: At יריחו the כהנים blew שופרות as they went around the city (יהושע 6).

phrases.english: And at יריחו there were שופרות,
so this is a refutation of the one who said 'with עננו'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין מִשֶּׁבַע תַּעֲנִיּוֹת עַל הַצִּבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the assumption from step 18 to attack the עננו view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of רב that the alarm is with עננו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's sign for fast-day alarms is יריחו, where שופרות were blown, so the alarm must involve שופרות, against a view that allows only עננו.

steps.title: The argument is only about עננו, not about שופרות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא retracts its earlier assumption. Everyone agrees שופרות count as הַתְרָעָה; the only argument is whether עננו also counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: everyone agrees that blowing שופרות is called 'sounding the alarm'. They argue only about עננו. One Sage holds it is also called 'sounding the alarm', and the other Sage holds it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the קשיא from יריחו by changing how it understands the argument between רב יהודה and רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 18 the גמרא assumed each side rejects the other's method. Now it says nobody rejects שופרות, so the יריחו sign, which is about שופרות, no longer refutes רב. The only open question is whether עננו also earns the name הַתְרָעָה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the גמרא is dropping its earlier assumption.

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides accept שופרות. The only argument is whether עננו is also called הַתְרָעָה.

phrases.english: Rather: with shofarot,
everyone does not disagree
that it is called 'sounding the alarm.'
When they disagree, it is about Aneinu.
One Sage holds: it is called 'sounding the alarm,'

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: לָא קָרֵי לַהּ הַתְרָעָה.
phrases.english: and one Sage holds: it is not called 'sounding the alarm.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: בְּשׁוֹפָרוֹת, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the יריחו קשיא of step 19 by rejecting the assumption made in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the scope of the argument
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each side rejects the other's method, so the עננו view rejects שופרות.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone accepts שופרות as הַתְרָעָה. The argument is only about whether עננו is also called הַתְרָעָה.

steps.title: What follows: עננו is the stronger response
steps.stepSummary: Under the new framing, the עננו view allows שופרות all the more so, while the שופרות view does not allow עננו. This implies that עננו is the greater response.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says the alarm is with עננו, all the more so with שופרות. According to the one who says it is with שופרות, it is not with עננו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws out what step 20 implies about how the two methods compare. This sets up the next challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the opinion that includes עננו accepts שופרות 'all the more so', then עננו must be the bigger step. The other opinion stops at שופרות and does not go up to עננו.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says
'Answer us', a special prayer for times of trouble

phrases.english: According to the one who says with Aneinu,
all the more so with shofarot.
And according to the one who says with shofarot,
but with Aneinu, no!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר בַּ״עֲנֵנוּ״ כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן בְּשׁוֹפָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out what follows from the reframing in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The עננו view includes שופרות all the more so; the שופרות view excludes עננו. So עננו is the more serious response.

steps.title: A ברייתא treats crying out as lesser than sounding the alarm
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that for lesser calamities they do not sound the alarm but cry out. Crying out is done with the mouth, so הַתְרָעָה must mean שופרות, which are kept for worse situations.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: for all other calamities that break out, such as scabs, locusts, flies, hornets, mosquitoes, or an outbreak of snakes and scorpions, they would not sound the alarm but would cry out. Since crying out is with the mouth, sounding the alarm must be with שופרות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 21 with a ברייתא that places prayer with the mouth below הַתְרָעָה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats 'crying out' (prayer with the mouth) as something other than הַתְרָעָה, and uses it for less serious troubles. That suggests prayer is not called הַתְרָעָה and is weaker than שופרות, which clashes with the view that עננו counts as הַתְרָעָה and is the stronger step.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught:
and all other kinds of calamities that break out,
for example: scabs, locusts,
flies, hornets, and mosquitoes,
and an outbreak of snakes and scorpions
they would not sound the alarm, but would cry out.
Since crying out is with the mouth,
sounding the alarm is with shofarot!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: וּשְׁאָר כׇּל מִינֵי פּוּרְעָנוּיוֹת הַמִּתְרַגְּשׁוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the framing of steps 20 and 21 using a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that prayer (עננו) is called הַתְרָעָה and is the stronger response.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא contrasts הַתְרָעָה with crying out by mouth and uses crying out for lesser troubles. So הַתְרָעָה means שופרות, and prayer is not called הַתְרָעָה.

steps.title: The question is an argument among the תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that whether crying out counts as הַתְרָעָה is itself argued by תנאים. It shows this from a משנה about sounding the alarm on שבת, where רבי יוסי allows it only to call for help, not for crying out.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is an argument of תנאים, as we learned in a משנה: for these they sound the alarm even on שבת: for a city surrounded by an army or a river, and for a ship tossed about at sea. רבי יוסי says: to call for help, but not for crying out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the ברייתא by saying it reflects only one side of an argument among the תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the first opinion allows הַתְרָעָה on שבת without limits, while רבי יוסי allows it only to call for help, not for crying out to ה׳. This shows the תנאים argued about how 'crying out' relates to הַתְרָעָה. The ברייתא follows one side, and the view that counts עננו as הַתְרָעָה can follow the other.

keyTerms.meaning: It is an argument among the תנאים
A ship being tossed about at sea

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא does not settle the matter. Whether crying out counts as הַתְרָעָה is argued by the תנאים, as the משנה and רבי יוסי show.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי does not reject sounding the alarm on שבת. He limits it to calling people for help and excludes crying out.

phrases.english: It is a dispute of tanna'im,
as we learned in a mishna:
For these they sound the alarm on Shabbat:

phrases.aramaic: עַל עִיר שֶׁהִקִּיפוּהָ גַּיִיס אוֹ נָהָר,
phrases.english: for a city surrounded by an army or a river,
phrases.notes: The river means a flood threatening the city.

phrases.english: and for a ship tossed about at sea.
Rabbi Yosei says:
to call for help, but not for crying out.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּאֵי הִיא, דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Argument among the תנאים: the challenging source follows only one opinion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא proves that prayer is never called הַתְרָעָה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנאים argue about crying out and הַתְרָעָה, as the first opinion and רבי יוסי in the משנה show. The ברייתא follows one side.

steps.title: With what did they sound the alarm on שבת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of alarm the שבת משנה means. It rules out שופרות, because blowing a שופר is not allowed on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: With what do they sound the alarm? If you say with שופרות, is blowing שופרות allowed on שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks closely at the משנה from the last step and asks what 'sounding the alarm' on שבת means. This sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה speaks of sounding the alarm on שבת. Blowing שופרות is not allowed on שבת, so the משנה cannot mean שופרות. That leaves only one other choice.

phrases.english: With what?
phrases.notes: He's asking what they sound the alarm with in the שבת משנה from the last step.

phrases.english: If you say with shofarot —
are shofarot permitted on Shabbat?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי? אִילֵימָא בְּשׁוֹפָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks closely at the שבת משנה quoted in step 23 to find out what kind of alarm it means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does 'sounding the alarm' on שבת mean in the משנה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not שופרות, since they are not allowed on שבת. The answer is given in the next step.

steps.title: So it must be עננו, and the משנה still calls it הַתְרָעָה
steps.stepSummary: Since it cannot be שופרות, the alarm on שבת must be the prayer עננו. The משנה calls this הַתְרָעָה, which proves that some תנא counts prayer as הַתְרָעָה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is it not with עננו? And the משנה still calls it הַתְרָעָה. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the alarm on שבת is the prayer עננו. That proves that some תנא calls prayer הַתְרָעָה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 22 a ברייתא made it look as if crying out with the mouth is not הַתְרָעָה. Here we see a תנא who does call prayer הַתְרָעָה. So the question is a disagreement between תנאים, and the עננו view still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not so that...
'Answer us', a prayer said in times of trouble
Learn from this; it is proven

steps.whatToRemember: The שבת משנה proves that a תנא counts the prayer עננו as הַתְרָעָה, so the עננו view has support among the תנאים.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not with "Aneinu"?
And it calls it sounding the alarm.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the שבת משנה. It uses the word הַתְרָעָה even though it is talking about prayer.

phrases.english: Conclude from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו, בַּ״עֲנֵנוּ״, וְקָרֵי לַהּ הַתְרָעָה, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the process of elimination begun in step 24 and closes the answer of step 23.
steps.raayaObject: That there is a תנא who counts prayer (עננו) as הַתְרָעָה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about sounding the alarm on שבת. Since שופרות are not allowed on שבת, the alarm there must be עננו, and the משנה still calls it הַתְרָעָה.

steps.title: A time of trouble in the days of רבי יהודה נשיאה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new story. In the years of רבי יהודה נשיאה, there was trouble.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the years of רבי יהודה נשיאה there was a trouble.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story about a time of trouble in the days of רבי יהודה נשיאה. This line only sets the scene for what comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic moves from the argument about הַתְרָעָה to a real event. The story will show how the community responded to trouble.

phrases.english: In the years of Rabbi Yehuda Nesia
there was a trouble,

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁנֵי דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה הֲוָה צַעֲרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story after the proof about הַתְרָעָה is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets the scene: there was trouble in the years of רבי יהודה נשיאה.
